Randomized trial in ambulatory/outpatient setting for type 2 diabetes. Intervention involves pharmacist-patient clinic visits with comprehensive medication review, monitoring, and counseling alongside physicians. This represents Team Changes (TC) - a system-targeted QI strategy where pharmacists work collaboratively with physicians and other providers.

Randomized trial in rural community setting for type 2 diabetes. However, CHW interventions consist mainly of home visits, health education, patient diary, and telephonic reminders - these are patient-targeted strategies (PE, PSM, PR) without clear system- or provider-targeted components. Does not meet criteria requiring at least one system/provider-targeted strategy.

Randomized trial but NOT primarily a diabetes study. Focuses on hypertensive men with multiple risk factors including cholesterol, smoking, OR diabetes. Diabetes was only one of several inclusion criteria, not the target population. Study objective centers on cardiovascular outcomes and intima-media thickness in hypertensive patients.

Randomized trial in outpatient setting for type 2 diabetes. Group visits represent a delivery modality change but primarily function as patient-targeted education/support. No clear system- or provider-targeted QI strategy (CM, TC, EPR, FR, CQI, AF, CE, CR, FI) identified in the intervention design.

Randomized trial in outpatient/clinic setting for diabetes patients. Intervention uses modem transfer of blood glucose data from patients to healthcare providers, representing Facilitated Relay of Clinical Information (FR) - a system-targeted QI strategy that enhances communication between patients and providers.

Randomized trial in outpatient setting for urban minority diabetes patients. Described as 'provider-assisted' telehealth self-management intervention, indicating provider involvement beyond pure patient education. Conservative inclusion due to provider assistance component suggesting system/provider engagement, though abstract lacks detail on specific QI strategies.

Randomized trial for type 2 diabetes but PRIMARY SETTING IS EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, not outpatient. Intervention targets hyperglycemic adults being discharged from ED to home. Selection criteria specifically require outpatient settings, which excludes ED-based interventions even if follow-up occurs in ambulatory setting.

Randomized trial in outpatient setting for type 2 diabetes. Intervention involves collaborative algorithm developed with clinicians (pharmacists, endocrinologists, nurses, family physicians) incorporating screening, education, and dose modification guidance. Represents Clinician Education (CE) - a provider-targeted QI strategy empowering healthcare providers with structured decision-making tools.

Randomized trial in community pharmacy (outpatient) setting for type 2 diabetes. Interventions delivered by pharmacists/pharmaconomists involving comprehensive medication review, problem identification, and individually tailored solutions. Represents Team Changes (TC) and/or Case Management (CM) - system/provider-targeted strategies expanding the care team to include pharmacists.

Cluster randomized trial in primary healthcare facilities (outpatient) for type 2 diabetes. Intervention explicitly includes 'additional case management' (ACM) with clinical care guide, pictorial flipbook for lifestyle education, clinician training, and mobile phone follow-up. Clearly meets criteria with Case Management (CM) and Clinician Education (CE) - both system/provider-targeted QI strategies.

This is a clinical trial evaluating a diagnostic monitoring strategy (routine HbA1c measurement) rather than a quality improvement programme. It does not explicitly test a system- or provider-targeted QI strategy (e.g., CM, TC, EPR, FR, CQI, AF, CE, CR, FI) as defined by the protocol.

Randomised trial in an outpatient setting comparing a nurse-led hypertension clinic to conventional care for type 2 diabetes. The nurse-led clinic model constitutes a team changes (TC) and/or case management (CM) strategy, meeting the selection criteria.

Randomised trial evaluating a pharmaceutical care model delivered by an experienced pharmacist versus standard pharmacy service. This represents a team changes (TC) or provider-targeted strategy aimed at improving medication adherence and glycemic control in an outpatient/hospital setting.

Cluster-randomised trial evaluating a blended psycho-educational intervention (HypoAware). This is solely a patient-targeted strategy (patient education/self-management). The protocol requires patient-targeted strategies to be combined with at least one system- or provider-targeted strategy, which is absent here.

Randomised controlled trial of a telemonitoring device that transmits patient readings to a diabetes care manager. This constitutes facilitated relay of clinical information (FR) and/or case management (CM), meeting the criteria for a system/provider-targeted QI strategy in an outpatient setting.

Randomised trial of an automated telemedicine monitoring system for insulin-treated diabetes. The remote monitoring and data transmission represent facilitated relay of clinical information (FR) or an electronic patient registry (EPR) strategy, qualifying as a system-targeted QI intervention.

System-wide randomised trial of chronic care clinics in primary care. The intervention includes standardized assessments, multidisciplinary visits (physician, nurse, pharmacist), and group education, encompassing team changes (TC), case management (CM), and patient education (PE) combined with provider strategies.

Randomised controlled trial of an automated Diabetes Remote Monitoring and Management System (DRMS). The system uses automated reminders and algorithm-based insulin adjustments, representing facilitated relay of clinical information (FR) and patient reminders (PR) integrated with a system-targeted strategy.

Cluster randomised controlled trial evaluating a government supervision programme involving inspections, site visits, and individualized reports for care groups. This constitutes audit and feedback (AF) and/or continuous quality improvement (CQI), meeting the provider/system-targeted criteria.

Randomised trial of multiple patient reminders for diabetic retinopathy screening. Crucially, physician groups also received letters with guidelines and patient lists, which constitutes clinician reminders (CR) or audit and feedback (AF). Thus, patient reminders are combined with a provider-targeted strategy, meeting the criteria.

RCT of a pharmacist-delivered intervention providing personalized treatment recommendations to PCPs via letter/EMR, functioning as a clinician reminder (CR) or facilitated relay (FR) for diabetes care in an outpatient primary care setting.
This is a Cochrane systematic review/meta-analysis of educational meetings across various healthcare conditions, not a primary randomized trial of a diabetes-specific QI program.
RCT evaluating a patient-targeted telephone coaching intervention for diabetes management. Lacks any system- or provider-targeted QI strategy as required by the selection criteria.

Pragmatic RCT evaluating practice-embedded nurse case management (CM) combined with motivational interviewing for high-risk type 2 diabetes patients in an outpatient setting, meeting the system-targeted strategy criterion.
RCT assessing self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) with or without patient instruction. This is a purely patient-targeted intervention without a required system- or provider-targeted component.
This is a Cochrane systematic review/meta-analysis of audit and feedback interventions across multiple clinical areas, not a primary randomized trial focused on diabetes QI.

Cluster-randomized trial implementing a QI program adapted from an integrated care system to improve guideline-concordant cardioprotective prescribing for diabetes in community health centers, involving system/provider-targeted strategies.
RCT testing a web-based self-management intervention for older adults with diabetes. This is a patient-targeted strategy without a concurrent system- or provider-targeted QI component.

RCT evaluating active care management (CM) supported by home telemonitoring and nurse practitioner medication adjustments for veterans with type 2 diabetes in primary care, meeting the system/provider-targeted criterion.

RCT comparing group-based rehabilitation to individual counseling for type 2 diabetes. Both arms are patient-targeted educational/behavioral interventions lacking system- or provider-targeted QI strategies.
RCT of diabetes care but intervention (Islamic Care Method) is patient-targeted education/behavior modification only, lacking system/provider-targeted QI strategy.
RCT of diabetes care but intervention (online self-tracking/Fitbit) is patient-targeted self-management tool only, lacking system/provider-targeted QI strategy.
RCT of diabetes care using group visits, but this is a care delivery model rather than a defined QI programme with system/provider-targeted strategies; no explicit QI methodology described.
RCT of diabetes QI programme in outpatient setting with Facilitated Relay of Clinical Information (FR) - video consultations with upload of measurements visible to patient and nurse.

RCT of diabetes QI programme in outpatient setting with Team Changes (TC), Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI via Breakthrough Series collaborative), and Electronic Patient Registry (EPR via clinical information systems).
RCT of diabetes care but intervention (self-management education program) is patient-targeted only, lacking system/provider-targeted QI strategy.
RCT of diabetes QI programme in outpatient setting with Team Changes (TC - medical team involvement) and Facilitated Relay of Clinical Information (FR - mHealth telemedicine with data transmission).
Cluster RCT of diabetes QI programme in general practice (outpatient) with Team Changes (TC - Asian link workers and extra community diabetes specialist nurse sessions).

RCT comparing two patient-targeted glucose monitoring systems (mobile phone vs Internet); while data transfer occurs, the intervention focuses on patient self-monitoring rather than system/provider-targeted QI strategy.

RCT of diabetes QI programme in outpatient setting with Team Changes (TC - multidisciplinary team including physician, pharmacist, dietician, educator, social worker) and Electronic Patient Registry (EPR - integrated care program with tracking).

RCT of mobile app with social networking and CBT for T2D. Intervention is primarily patient-targeted (self-management support via app). No system/provider-targeted QI strategy (CM, TC, EPR, FR, CQI, AF, CE, CR, FI) identified.

RCT of telecare (glucometer data transmission with clinician feedback) for type 1 diabetes in outpatient setting. Clinician feedback component represents facilitated relay of clinical information (FR), a system-targeted QI strategy.
This is an overview of systematic reviews, not a primary randomised trial. Does not meet the study design criterion (must be RCT).

RCT testing mailings, appointment reminders, and telephone follow-up for diabetic patients. These are patient reminders (PR) - a patient-targeted strategy only. No system/provider-targeted QI strategy identified.

RCT comparing home telemedicine with standard outpatient care for diabetes. Intervention includes nurse case manager contacting patients weekly under physician direction, representing case management (CM), a system-targeted QI strategy.

Cluster RCT evaluating physician-pharmacist collaboration for blood pressure control in patients with uncontrolled hypertension. Wrong population - focuses on hypertension, not diabetes care.

RCT of supervised pharmacy student-led medication reviews for type 2 diabetes in primary care. Students integrated into medical practice to provide consultations represents team changes (TC), a system-targeted QI strategy.

RCT of pharmacist-led patient education program for type 2 diabetes in outpatient clinics. Pharmacist involvement in multidisciplinary teams with follow-up represents team changes (TC), a system-targeted QI strategy.

RCT of diabetic meal delivery vs dietary counseling vs conventional education for type 2 diabetes. All interventions are patient-targeted (dietary education/counseling). No system/provider-targeted QI strategy identified.

Randomized trial comparing telemedicine vs traditional eye exams for diabetic retinopathy screening in primary care clinics. Telemedicine represents facilitated relay of clinical information (FR) - a system-targeted QI strategy.
Randomized controlled trial testing physician education (clinician education - CE) and patient education for diabetes outcomes. Physician education is a provider-targeted QI strategy.
Not a randomized trial. Uses \'repeated measures pretest, post-test control group design\' which is a quasi-experimental design, not randomization.

Randomized trial of shared medical appointments (SMAs) for Hispanic patients with diabetes in a family medicine residency clinic. SMAs represent team changes (TC) - a system-targeted QI strategy that modifies how providers deliver care.

While randomized and involving diabetes patients, the intervention consists only of patient-targeted strategies (pedometer use and cognitive-behavioral group sessions) without any system- or provider-targeted QI strategy. Setting is also not clearly outpatient.
